ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Higuchi Ichiyō

text.paragraph: Ms. Higuchi returns having completed treatment five days ago: all 182 doses were observed by video, 56 in the intensive phase and 126 in the continuation phase, with none missed. The two-month sputum culture showed no growth. She has had no cough, fever or night sweats for four months and has gained 5.5 kg since intake. She has had no nausea, yellowing, numbness or change in vision. The cystitis in the summer did not return. The public health center has told her that its contact investigation is complete. She writes each morning and has finished two stories since the summer. Her cervical cytology was normal. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 44.0 kg, BMI 20.1; temperature 36.5 °C, pulse 72, blood pressure 106/68
Normal sensation and reflexes in the feet

Cough for about seven weeks with evening fevers, night sweats, poor appetite and weight loss of about 4 kg (about 10 percent) in a woman of 23; chest X-ray with patchy right upper lobe opacities and no cavity; suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; airborne precautions and three sputum specimens for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification and culture
S — Synthetic presenting problem at intake, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit; its timing echoes her documented decline from early 1896 (D).
Pulmonary tuberculosis of the right upper lobe, sputum smear-negative, confirmed by Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected, low; rifampin resistance not detected)
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; all bacteriology and imaging are synthetic.
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6, about 10 percent weight loss in two months, and albumin 3.3 g/dL
S — Synthetic nutrition diagnosis at intake, anchored to her documented poverty.
Low and irregular income from writing, with a household to support; costs of care are a barrier
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and household responsibilities.
Acute uncomplicated cystitis, treated with nitrofurantoin rather than a fluoroquinolone during tuberculosis treatment; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Pulmonary tuberculosis, treatment completed (A15.0). Treatment completed with full observed adherence, culture conversion by two weeks, clinical cure, and normal liver tests throughout. The chest X-ray shows the right upper lobe opacities cleared, leaving a few linear scars; it is kept as her new baseline. Relapse after a fully observed course for drug-susceptible disease is uncommon, so no routine sputum follow-up is needed. [S]
Stop isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine.
Return for a cough lasting more than two to three weeks, fevers, night sweats or weight loss, and tell future clinicians she has been treated for tuberculosis.
The orange color of urine and tears will fade within days.
Hormonal contraception becomes reliable again about four weeks after the last rifampin dose.

Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition, resolved (E44.0). Weight 44.0 kg, BMI 20.1, albumin 4.2 g/dL, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL. [S]
Stop the supplement drinks; keep three meals a day.

Low income (Z59.6). Public funding has ended with treatment; she has paid her clinic charges in instalments. [S]
Social worker review of her health insurance premiums and any further help.

list.item: Complete 182 daily doses within about six and a half months by video-observed therapy. Outcome by 2026-10-20: All 182 doses completed in 26 weeks: 56 in the intensive phase and 126 in the continuation phase, none missed [S]
Sputum culture negative at two months. Outcome by 2026-10-20: The cultures taken at two weeks and at two months both showed no growth after six weeks [S]
Weight at least 44 kg (BMI about 20) by the end of treatment. Outcome by 2026-10-20: 44.0 kg at the end of treatment, from 38.5 kg at intake [S]

Keep writing on a paced schedule without losing income during treatment. Outcome by 2026-10-20: Public funding covered most treatment costs; she kept writing about two hours a day and finished new work [S]
No drug-induced liver injury or loss of vision during treatment. Outcome by 2026-10-20: Liver tests normal throughout; visual acuity unchanged [S]
